newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Strong gains on busy day for IPOs.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Strong gains on busy day for IPOs.

text.p: Seven companies went public on Thursday, with Metro Information Services Inc, SCPIE Holdings Inc and Doncasters Plc posting impressive gains.

Metro Information shares jumped 21 percent, or 3-3/8, to 19-3/8 in heavy Nasdaq trading. The IPO had been forecast as one of the hottest deals of the week. The 3.1 million shares priced at the top of their range of $15 to $16, according to lead underwriter Robert Baird & Co.
The Virginia Beach, Va., company provides information technology services.
Of the 3.1 million shares offered, Metro Information sold 2.3 million and 800,000 were sold by Chairman Jahn Fain, cutting his stake to 56.9 percent from 73.7 percent.
SCPIE shares rose 2-1/2 to 20-3/4 from the IPO price of 18-1/4, which was below the estimated price range of $19 to $21. The company provides medical malpractice insurance.
Doncasters jumped 21 percent in heavy early trading, rising 3-3/8 to 19-7/8. The company was spun off by Canadian mining company Inco Ltd.
Although demand was strong for the top three gainers, it remained selective and did not necessarily broaden out to other IPOs.
Two deals, Epix Medical Inc and Medical Manager Corp, priced below their estimated price ranges, and others barely eked out gains.
Other companies that made their IPO debuts Thursday:
-- National Auto Finance Co Inc shares rose to 9-3/4 from their IPO price of $8.50.
-- Epix Medical shares inched up 1/2 to 7-1/2. The Cambridge, Mass., company offered two million shares that priced at $7, below their range of $9-$11.
-- Medical Manager shares edged up 1/8 to 11-1/8. The Tampa, Fla., company offers comprehensive physician practice management systems.

-- Medialink Worldwide shares rose 1/2 to 9-1/2. The shares priced at the low end of their IPO price range of $9-$11. Dean Witter Reynolds was the lead underwriter of the offering of two million shares, all sold by the company.

Medialink provides video and audio production services for businesses to make "video news releases" to be integrated into newscasts. It said its materials have appeared on ABC, CBS, NBC and their affiliates as well as CNN and CNBC.
